source_text:
Λογικὴ ἄρα, καὶ ταῖς ψυχαῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὁμοούσιος, ὥσπερ καὶ ἡ σὰρξ ὁμοούσιος τῇ τῶν
ἀνθρώπων σαρκὶ τυγχάνει, ἐκ τῆς Μαρίας προελθοῦσα.
thought_title: The soul and flesh of Jesus are of the same substance as human souls and flesh
orientation: Eustathius is concluding his argument that the soul of Jesus is rational and of the same substance as human souls, just as his flesh is of the same substance as human flesh, having come from Mary.
pass_a_gloss: Rational therefore, and of the same substance as the souls of human beings, just as also the flesh is of the same substance as the flesh of human beings, having come forth from Mary.

choices.why: The adjective is fronted for emphasis, continuing the previous section's point about the soul's rational nature; 'therefore' draws the conclusion from the preceding argument.

choices.english: of the same substance as the souls of human beings
choices.why: The glossary requires 'of the same substance' for ὁμοούσιος and 'soul' for ψυχή; the dative with ὁμοούσιος expresses the comparison.
rejected: of one being with the souls of men

choices.term: ὥσπερ καὶ ἡ σὰρξ ὁμοούσιος τῇ τῶν ἀνθρώπων σαρκὶ τυγχάνει
choices.english: just as also the flesh is of the same substance as the flesh of human beings
choices.why: The ὥσπερ clause draws a parallel between soul and flesh; τυγχάνει is a copula-like verb meaning 'is' here, and the dative σαρκὶ marks the comparison.
rejected: just as the flesh happens to be of the same substance as human flesh
as the flesh also is consubstantial with the flesh of men

choices.why: The participle is feminine singular, agreeing with σάρξ; προελθοῦσα means 'having come forth' or 'having proceeded,' indicating origin from Mary.

pass_b_english: Therefore the soul of Jesus is rational and of the same substance as the souls of human beings, just as his flesh is of the same substance as human flesh, having come forth from Mary.
